prediction_question: For a complaint submitted to the CFPB Consumer Complaint Database, will the company close it with monetary or non-monetary relief rather than explanation alone?
prediction_time: At complaint intake: the consumer-submitted narrative plus product, issue, sub-issue, company, state, ZIP, submitted-via channel and date are known; the company response (the label) is filed later by the company in its CFPB portal response.
target_definition: Binary from the documented company_response_to_consumer field: positive if the response is 'Closed with monetary relief' or 'Closed with non-monetary relief', negative for 'Closed with explanation' and administrative closures. timely_response is a separate documented outcome, not used.

rejection_reason: Equivalent already exists in usable form, so per the standing novelty test this is a rejection, not a candidate. The exact intake-time-to-outcome task is published and de-risked by third parties: (1) arXiv 2606.22664 'Sub-Issue Vs. % Of Replies' builds binary monetary-relief classification on CFPB complaint data with narrative text, LDA topics, engineered text features and structured fields (company, state), XGBoost, a temporal train/test split, AUC-ROC 0.78 vs a 0.69 TF-IDF baseline - i.e. the task, the leakage discipline (intake-time features only) and the temporal-split protocol are all already public; (2) 'Customer complaint analytics in digital financial services' (Future Business Journal, 2026) predicts subsequent untimely company responses from intake-time information with a chronological holdout, ROC AUC 0.7653; (3) github.com/RishiRatnakarData/consumer-complaint-intelligence ships an end-to-end intake-time-only, leakage-aware classifier (relief rate 40.6%, chronological 75/25 split, company-level relief rates measured); (4) Yale SOM / Jiwoong Shin et al. analyse 1.1M+ complaints for relief outcomes vs LLM-written narratives. What exists: the source, the task, intake-time feature discipline and temporal splits, all public. What would be ours: only re-partitioning and packaging - a mirror, not a contribution.
next_action: None - dropped on novelty (2026-10-19). Do not reopen for outcome prediction from intake-time fields. Reopening would only make sense for a materially different task (e.g. cross-firm panel analysis rather than per-complaint outcome), which would be a new candidate with its own novelty search.
